# Summary of Cairn Mechanics

## Pulses
A pulse represents growth. You start with a base amount called the stride, which always gets added. Then you calculate a bonus based on how tall the cairn has become: you divide the new height (after adding stride) by the stride value and take the floor. That bonus gets added too. So taller cairns generate larger bonuses—creating accelerating growth.

## Repeated Pulses
Simply apply the pulse rule multiple times in sequence. Each cycle uses the height from the previous cycle as the starting point. The bonuses tend to grow larger with each pulse since the cairn gets taller.

## Leaks
A leak is proportional loss—it scales with height. You calculate how many complete leak-sized chunks fit into your current height and lose that many marks. Smaller cairns lose less; taller ones lose more. This creates a natural balance preventing infinite growth.

## Drains
Unlike leaks, drains are fixed losses—the same amount every cycle regardless of height. This can be dangerous for shrinking cairns, as the drain stays constant while bonus growth diminishes, creating a potential death spiral.

## Merging Cairns
Two cairns combine using weighted shares (typically percentages that sum to 100%). You calculate each contribution, sum them, then apply a tether adjustment based on the shorter cairn. The tether divisor determines how much bonus or penalty applies.

## Finding Origins
Work backwards by testing guess heights and simulating forward through all cycles. When the simulation matches the known result, you've found the origin.
